correctness.rationale: On support S, psi(m)-m=m(A_S/D_S), with A_S=product(p+1)-product(p), D_S=product p. Product balance around an r-cycle is necessary and excludes all new primes outside the prescribed support union. For each prime, all r valuations are initial valuation plus the stated integer shifts h_i,p. A zero valuation at any absent step uniquely fixes its starting exponent; primes present everywhere require only a sharp lower bound and so contribute independent nonnegative exponent shifts. Reconstructing the rational orbit from these shifts checks integrality, support and return after r steps. For a repeated shorter word of length s, its positive multiplier product c obeys c^(r/s)=1, hence c=1 and exact dynamical period is s. Counting lattice points in the weighted simplex sum t_p log p <= log(X/n*) yields the volume leading term and O(Y^(d-1)) boundary error. This reasoning covers r=1, rank0, nonprimitive words, and arbitrary primes and exponents.
residual_risks: The direct finite search through n<=25000 is corroboration only; all-length result rests on the valuation and weighted-simplex arguments.

value.rationale: This is a natural conditional exact periodic-orbit problem left unaddressed by aggregate density theorems. It supplies a complete finite decision algorithm for a specified cyclic prime-divisor itinerary, explicit canonical generator, dimension of its infinite family, correct distinction between primitive and repeated itinerary lengths, and quantitatively sharp per-fiber point count. The examples reveal why product balance alone is insufficient. The result is not advertised as solving existence of cycles of unrestricted lengths.
residual_risks: No uniform count across all words; precise implication is conditional on fixed support word.

final_claim: For any fixed finite ordered nonempty prime-support itinerary of positive periodic points of T(n)=psi(n)-n, the exact fiber is empty or n_* times a free multiplicative lattice of powers of the primes present at every step; cyclic support-word and exact dynamical least periods coincide; for persistent-prime rank d the fixed-fiber point count has explicit polylogarithmic main term and O((1+log X)^(d-1)) remainder.
